<reason>Both sides ran disciplined, on-motion cases. A's ratchet mechanism was well built and its sharpest hit — that published discounts (student/senior fares) survive disclosure only because they carry a verification gate that algorithmic signals lack — genuinely damaged B's central empirical analogy, and A's turn on the midnight-plumber example (time-of-night is a sale condition, i.e. outside PRO's own line) went largely unanswered. But B controlled the decisive clash on two fronts. First, B attacked the causal premise of A's welfare story: the algorithm sorts by willingness and urgency, not ability to pay, so the "rescued price-sensitive buyer" may be the trapped buyer, not the poor one. A never squarely answered this, and instead conceded in [A4.1] that the unsophisticated already pay the most today — which B converted in closing into a concession that CON is defending the status quo harm. Second, B's fork ("if the low price survives naming, disclosure is free; if it dies, it was revenue harvested from ignorance") forced A into defending concealment as such, and A's admission that it does not defend lying when asked left it protecting only "a firm's right to hope you never ask." B also handled A's strongest pressure (enforceability, criteria-gaming) with concrete, plausible answers — the swap test with shadow shoppers and a two-tier aggregate-disclosure-plus-right-to-ask regime — which blunts the spoofing collapse A relied on in closing. B's clipped rebuttal is a real but small execution cost, since the lost weighing was restated later. Net: B narrowed and resolved the clash more cleanly.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's fork plus its exploitation of A's [A4.2] concession: once A admitted it would not defend lying to a customer who asks, and admitted in [A4.1] that the unsophisticated already pay the most today, B's "either the low price survives being named, or it was harvested from ignorance" left CON defending a subsidy that dies on contact with truth. A's counter — that disclosure itself manufactures the collapse by teaching the sophisticated what to spoof — was the best available reply but was partly pre-empted by B's aggregate-disclosure-without-criteria design.</best_rebuttal>
